task.target: 33 'Interior anchor' addresses published by the SWE2-EC7-20/21/22 pass are not instruction boundaries, and the prose written around them describes instruction streams the shipped bodies do not contain.

task.question: From what offset were the SWE2-EC7-20/21/22 windows decoded, and which of the 33 mid-instruction paragraphs should be withdrawn versus re-derived from the entry?
task.original_claim: SWE2-EC7-20 update, CONTRACT-render-record-pool-lifecycle.md: '0051F9F0 (380 B window) is the descriptor writer's arm cluster ... per-arm float writes [rdx+0x3C]/+0x44/+0x4C/+0x50 ... Interior anchor 0051F9F2 (the movups arm head)'; and '0051FF30 (217 B window) is the descriptor linked-list refresh arm: [r14+0x10] float staged with the 0199C990 constant ... call 0020D600 twice ... Interior anchor 0051FF3B (the float load)'. Sixteen further paragraphs in the same three passes carry the same shape.
task.counter_evidence: MECHANISM. x86-64 is not self-synchronising: a decode starting one or two bytes late produces a fluent but fictional instruction stream. Every one of the 33 flagged anchors is INSIDE an instruction rather than at its start. 0051F9F0's entry instruction is 48 89 5C 24 08, spanning 0051F9F0-0051F9F4, so the quoted anchor 0051F9F2 is two bytes into it; 0051FF30's entry is 40 53 (push rbx) and 0051FF3B falls inside 8B 79 40 at 0051FF39. BYTES. Disassembling both bodies in full from their graph entries: 0051F9F0 (380 B, 100 instructions) contains ZERO SSE or float instructions of any kind and no write through rdx at all - rdx carries the immediate 0x260 and is stored to [rbx+0x48]; the +0x4C and +0x50 writes are integer (r8d = bank shift 5, and eax = (1<<shift)-1, the index mask). 0051FF30 (217 B) likewise contains ZERO SSE instructions, never references [r14+0x10] (its only r14 dereference is [r14+8], the next-index link), never mentions 0199C990, and calls 003AB7F0/0020E600/r15 - there is no call to 0020D600. What the two functions actually are: 0051F9F0 initialises a chunked slot container's storage (rowStride, bank shift, index mask, total slots, the live-list head/tail = -1, and one heap block of totalSlots*rowStride at 0051FAFE), and 0051FF30 walks that container's live list calling a caller-supplied callback per element. FIVE MORE VERIFIED BY HAND, all fictional: 00609710 is described as 'and al,0x50 mask + mov rcx,r14 continuation into the shared tail' but its 7 bytes are 'mov eax,[rcx+8]; and eax,1; ret' - it returns, there is no continuation; 0041C760 is described as 'mov ebx,0x280FFFFE mask constant + and al,0x50' but its 14 bytes are 'mov eax,[rcx+0x2C8]; shr rax,0xC; and eax,1; ret'; 0060E7A0 is described with an 'xmm1=[rdx] float comiss > 0' gating a 'cmova' into '[r8+0x28]' but its 98 bytes contain zero SSE, zero cmova and neither [rcx+0x38] nor [r8+0x28]; 0060CE50 is called 'a mid-body fragment' but 0060CE50 is a function entry with a standard prologue (mov [rsp+8],rbx; push rbp; lea rbp,[rsp-0x57]; sub rsp,0xB0), and neither the 'shr eax,1' nor any [r11+0x28/0x2C/0x30/0x10/0x14] it describes occurs in its 827 bytes; 00409600 (ResourceEntry_GetResolvedBasePointer, a NAMED function other contracts depend on) is described as 'a six-slot lea rax,[rip+...] / mov [rip+0x286CBxx],rax block publishing handler pointers to the 02D3xxxx global table', but its 86 bytes are a mode dispatch on [rcx+4]: mode 0 tail-jumps 0051EE00 with rbx+0x10, mode 1 returns the cached [rbx+0x38] unless the global byte at 02B62E10 is set, in which case it re-resolves [rbx+0x30] through 003AB7F0 and re-caches. There is no lea/rip publish block and no reference to 02D3xxxx anywhere in the body. THE CHECK. Database/Tools/analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/check_interior_anchors.py decodes each named function from its graph entry and reports anchors that are not instruction starts; it self-tests on one boundary anchor (004090A3, from EC7-22, which is correct) and one mid-instruction anchor (0051F9F2). Corpus: 176 anchors checked, 143 on a boundary, 33 mid-instruction, 0 unmapped. NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT: a boundary anchor does not make a paragraph right - 001823B0's anchor 001823B9 is a real 'test rax,rax' and its paragraph still describes a mod-4 index sequence absent from that 46-byte body (which is 'sub rsp,0x28; call 0018CA40; test rax,rax; ...; jmp 0018BE70'). So 33 is a floor on the affected paragraphs, not the count.

task.missing_information: Whether the misalignment is a fixed offset or varies per entry (the flagged anchors sit +1 to +13 into their bodies, which argues against one constant skew); whether the SAME misaligned windows also produced the caller lists and byte counts (those check out against the graph, so probably not); and whether EC7 passes before -20 share the defect - this census covers every 'Interior anchor' string in the database, so any earlier affected text either uses different wording or is among the 143 that pass.
task.why_it_matters: This is published contract text in seventeen documents across twelve subsystems, and at least one affected body (00409600 ResourceEntry_GetResolvedBasePointer) is a NAMED function that other contracts already build on. A reader reconstructing from these paragraphs writes float pipelines, mask constants and publish blocks that do not exist in the shipped image - the failure is not a wrong detail but a plausible invented body, which is the hardest kind to catch downstream. SWE2-CONTRACT independently hit one instance of the same pass (SWE2-CONTRACT-REQ-EC7-PHYRE-LEA-QUOTE, the 005CD0E0 quote in CONTRACT-phyre-cluster-header.md); that request and this contradiction are the same defect at two scales, and 005CD0E0's anchor is NOT among the 33, so wrong-body quotes and misaligned decodes are two distinct symptoms of it.
task.what_is_blocked: Nothing of OPUS's own: 0051F9F0/0051FF30 are re-read from the bytes and RenderModelInstance's lifetime is closed on that reading, not on the EC7 text. Blocked for others: any reconstruction or contract exercise that quotes an affected paragraph, and the standing of the SWE2-EC7-20/21/22 sections as evidence.
task.known_evidence: check_interior_anchors.py (new, self-tested on one correct and one wrong anchor from the same pass) decodes each named body from its graph entry and reports Interior anchor addresses that are not instruction starts: 176 checked, 143 on a boundary, 33 MID-INSTRUCTION, 0 unmapped. Eight of the 33 were then read by hand against the shipped image and all eight paragraphs describe instructions the bodies do not contain; the full disassembly evidence is in counter_evidence.
